Plot a batch correction

Source: R/batch_correct.r
plot.ecodive_batch.Rd

MMUPHin's diagnostic figure for a corrected table, in base graphics: how far the empirical Bayes step shrank each batch effect, and each feature's batch means before and after the correction.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_batch'
plot(x, type = c("shrinkage", "means"), legend = "topleft", ...)

Arguments

x

The result of batch_mmuphin() or batch_combat().

type

"shrinkage" (the default): each feature's location effect in each batch, \(\hat\gamma\) (x), against its shrunken value \(\gamma^*\) (y), coloured by batch, with the 1:1 line. Points below the line in the upper right (and above it in the lower left) were pulled towards the batch's average effect. "means": for each feature (one vertical line of points per feature), its mean in each batch (y) against its mean over all samples (x), before the correction (black) and after (red, just to the right), with the 1:1 line. A batch effect spreads a feature's batch means away from the line; the correction draws them together. batch_mmuphin()'s means are of relative abundances; batch_combat()'s are of the values it corrected.

legend

Where to put the legend: a position keyword for graphics::legend() (such as "topleft"), or NULL for none. Default: "topleft".

...

Passed on to graphics::plot(), such as main, xlab, ylab, log, pch, cex, col ("shrinkage": one colour per batch; "means": before and after).

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

The plot reads only the attributes stored with the result, so a table taken apart with [ can't be plotted. The real check of a correction is an ordination coloured by batch, and the PERMANOVA \(R^2\) of batch, before and after (see the examples of batch_mmuphin()).

See also

batch_mmuphin(), batch_combat()

Examples

    set.seed(1)
    counts <- matrix(rpois(20 * 30, 20), 20, 30)
    batch  <- rep(c('run1', 'run2'), each = 10)
    counts[11:20, 1:10] <- counts[11:20, 1:10] * 3

    x <- batch_mmuphin(counts, batch)
    plot(x)

    plot(x, type = 'means')
